advances: Already for n=d=q=1, the example refutes a per-piece local-depth strengthening of integer-centroid partition existence. The original body satisfies the sharp bound at the middle-fiber midpoint, so it also satisfies the locked weak bound.

proof:
The three integer fiber intervals of $C$ are $[0,1]$, $[0,2]$ and $[0,3]$. The total mass is $6$ and the base first moment is $8$. One piece would have base centroid $4/3$. With two pieces the integer base means are distinct elements of $\{0,1,2\}$, since their weighted average is $4/3$. The pair $\{0,1\}$ cannot give this average. The pair $\{0,2\}$ would leave the middle fiber uncovered up to null sets, because a measure on these three bases with an extreme mean is supported on that extreme base. Thus the means are $1$ and $2$, with corresponding masses $m_D,m_E$ satisfying $m_D+m_E=6$ and $m_D+2m_E=8$. Hence $m_D=4$ and $m_E=2$.

The base-two piece has zero mass at bases $0$ and $1$, so $D$ contains the entire original intervals at these bases. Indeed the traces of a closed convex subset of $C$ are closed intervals (allowing points or the empty set), and full length forces equality with the original interval. At base $2$, the length-one trace $D_2$ and the length-two trace $E_2$ cover $[0,3]$ up to null sets and have null overlap. Their union is closed and therefore covers the whole interval. Ordering these two intervals from left to right forces
$$
(D_2,E_2)=([0,1],[1,3])\quad\text{or}\quad([2,3],[0,2]).
$$

In the first case the continuous first moment in $D$ is $1/2+2+1/2=3$, so $y_D=(1,3/4)$. The closed halfspace $H=\{x+4(z-1)\le3/4\}$ has boundary through $y_D$ and captures lengths $(1,3/4,0)$ on the three original fibers. In the second case the continuous first moment is $1/2+2+5/2=5$, so $y_D=(1,5/4)$. The closed halfspace $H=\{x-4(z-1)\ge5/4\}$ again passes through $y_D$ and captures lengths $(1,3/4,0)$. In both cases those lengths are entirely in $D$ up to mixed null sets. The first two fibers carry no $E$-mass, and the halfspaces miss the last original fiber. Dividing $7/4$ by $m_D=4$ proves the local depth bound.

The first trace pattern is realized by intersecting $C$ with the two closed sides of $x+z=3$. Take $D$ on the side $x+z\le3$. The second is realized by the two closed sides of $x-2z=-2$, with $D$ on the side $x-2z\ge-2$. In each case there are strict points on both sides in the interior of $C$. The two closed pieces cover $C$ and intersect in a line meeting each integer fiber in at most a point.

For comparison, the original midpoint $y=(1,1)$ of the middle fiber has raw depth exactly $2$. A halfspace containing $y$ may be translated inward until its boundary contains $y$. A through-$y$ halfspace with positive $x$ coefficient has the form $x-1+a(z-1)\ge0$, with original mass $1+[-a]_0^1+[2+a]_0^3$, where $[t]_0^b=\max(0,\min(b,t))$. As a function of $t=-a$, the outer contribution $[t]_0^1+[2-t]_0^3$ is nonincreasing. Its successive slopes on the intervals cut by $-1,0,1,2$ are $0,-1,0,-1,0$, with extreme values $3$ and $1$. Thus these halfspaces have masses in $[2,4]$, and $a=-2$ attains $2$. The opposite orientation has the complementary mass because the boundary cuts each integer fiber in at most a point. Through-$y$ halfspaces with zero $x$ coefficient are $\{z\le1\}$ and $\{z\ge1\}$, of masses $3$ and $5$. Consequently the original normalized depth at $y$ is $1/3$, and the caps proving the local obstruction have original mass $7/4>6\cdot2^{-1}\gamma_1=3/2$.
statement:
Let $C=\{(z,x)\in\mathbb R^2:0\le z\le2,\ 0\le x\le z+1\}$ and let $\mu$ be the restriction of $\mathcal H_1$ to $C\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R)$, equivalently the sum of the lengths on the three integer fibers. Suppose at most two closed convex subsets of $C$, each of positive $\mu$-mass, partition the mixed set up to $\mu$-null omissions and overlaps, and each has a true mixed centroid with integer base coordinate. Then there are exactly two pieces, $D$ and $E$, of masses $4$ and $2$ and base centroid coordinates $1$ and $2$, respectively. The true mixed centroid $y_D=\mu(D)^{-1}\int_D (z,x)\,d\mu$ lies on the boundary of a closed ambient halfspace $H$ with $\mu(D\cap H)=7/4$ and $\mu(E\cap H)=0$. Hence its normalized halfspace depth in $D$ is at most $7/16<\gamma_1=1/2$.

Such partitions exist even with full-dimensional pieces covering all of $C$. This body therefore disproves the assertion that every mixed-integer convex body admits an exhaustive partition into at most $2^n$ positive-mass closed convex pieces whose true mixed centroids have integer bases and each have normalized depth at least $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ within their own pieces.
title: Two integer-centroid convex pieces can fail the local Grünbaum bound
